title: Victim missed court appearance hours before being shot by police
article: A young man shot and killed by Hamilton police was scheduled to make a routine court appearance just hours before his death.

According to court documents, Phonesay Chanthachak was to appear at the John Sopinka Courthouse at 9 a.m. Monday. He was facing 18 charges that had stacked up over several months, including break and enter, identity theft and credit card theft.
When the 27-year-old - nicknamed Pun - missed his scheduled appearance, court officials say a warrant was issued for his arrest.
Four hours later he was dead.
Chanthachak, whose name is spelled "Chanthachack" on court documents, was shot on Quigley Road, several metres south of Albright Road, in east Hamilton.
The victim\'s van crashed into a hydro pole, kitty corner to Bishop Ryan Catholic Secondary School and right in front of Fire EMS Station No. 7.

Witnesses in the area said they heard two "bangs" or "pops," and then watched as the beige van mounted the sidewalk and smashed into the pole. The van also appeared to have bullet holes in the windshield, while the passenger window was shattered. The airbag had deployed and there was blood on the bag and the driver\'s seat.
Since the shooting involved police, the province\'s Special Investigations Unit (SIU) has gotten involved.
Chanthachak\'s family says it has been told little about the circumstances surrounding his death.
The SIU say Hamilton police have told them officers were in the Quigley and Albright road areas conducting a criminal investigation.
Officers attempted to stop a vehicle, there was "an interaction" between the officers and the victim and an officer discharged his gun.
Chanthachak was taken to Hamilton General Hospital, where he was pronounced dead.
Chanthachak\'s half-brother Paul told The Spectator that his sibling was the father of a six-year-old girl. The mother of the child, Natasha Thompson, was too distraught to talk on Tuesday.
"I don\'t want to comment right now," she said at her Greenhill Avenue apartment building, just around the corner from the shooting scene. "I\'m with the family."
Paul Chanthachak said his brother came to Canada from Laos with his family when he was three years old. The family included his parents, two brothers and a younger sister.
After several years in Manitoba, the family settled in Hamilton, where Phonesay attended Sir John A. Macdonald High School.
"He was a nice kid," said Paul. "People liked him."

Phonesay Chanthachak also liked to play basketball, his brother said. He still remembers the time "Pun" hit his head shooting hoops and had to be taken to Hamilton General - the same hospital where he was pronounced dead.

According to Paul, his brother had been working at York Barbell Co. Ltd., an Oakville sporting goods manufacturer, for the past year or so. He also said his brother had begun "hanging with the wrong group," but wouldn\'t elaborate.
A spokesperson from the South Service Road business could not be reached for comment.
Paul said the victim\'s parents, with whom Phonesay Chanthachak lived off and on, are upset by his death, but the family understands there are few details at the "early" stage of the investigation.

Hoowar Mahi, 25, is the owner of The Pizza House at the Quigley Road Plaza, which is metres from the shooting scene. He said the victim was a regular customer and had been coming into his business since he bought it in 2009.
Mahi called him "a very nice guy, seriously. He was very respectful. He was very friendly."

Chanthachak used to live in the building at 55 Tindale Ct., behind the shop, and Mahi said his death has upset the community. A superintendent at the building said Chanthachak had not lived in the building for five years, but was often there visiting friends.
"Everybody knew him here," said Mahi, adding that Chanthachak was in his store for a slice of pizza only last Friday and also tried to sell him a cellphone.
"Everyone is talking about him. Everybody is saying they had no right to kill the guy."
Mahi said Chanthachak often came into the store with his daughter.
"If he didn\'t have that much money on him, he would always buy a slice for his daughter," he added.

Mahi said he saw SIU vehicles leave the shooting scene at about 1 a.m. Tuesday. Hamilton police still kept the scene closed, but took down yellow tape and opened the intersection to traffic shortly after 5 p.m.
The SIU has identified one subject officer and three witness officers in relation to the incident. It has assigned seven investigators and three forensic investigators to the case.
Hamilton police have refused to comment, other than to say officers were in the area on a criminal investigation.
